name: Divided Kingdom and the Prophets

objectives.text: Identify Elijah as the prophet God sent to call Israel back to Him and recall that God answered Elijah with fire on Mount Carmel
Retell how God cared for Elijah through the ravens and the widow's flour and oil
Retell the story of Jonah, including God's call to Nineveh, Jonah's running away, the great fish, and God's mercy to the city
Recall that after Solomon the kingdom split into Israel in the north and Judah in the south
Identify a prophet as a messenger whom God sent to speak His words to His people
Retell how the foreign commander Naaman was healed of leprosy through the prophet Elisha
Summarize the contest on Mount Carmel and explain what it showed about the LORD and Baal
Describe, using examples of specific kings, how kings who did evil led the people to idols and kings who did right led them back to the LORD
Retell how young King Josiah responded when the Book of the Law was found in the temple
Explain why the kingdom divided, including Rehoboam's harsh answer and God's judgment on Solomon's idolatry
Describe how God met the discouraged Elijah at Horeb and told him of the seven thousand who had not bowed to Baal
Compare the Northern Kingdom of Israel and the Southern Kingdom of Judah by capital, ruling families, centers of worship, and length of existence
Locate Samaria, Jerusalem, Bethel, Dan, Mount Carmel, and Nineveh on a map of the divided kingdom period
Categorize the prophets of this period by whom they addressed, whether Israel, Judah, or other nations
Explain what the ending of Jonah teaches about God's compassion toward the nations and about Jonah's resistance to it
Analyze Jeroboam's golden calves as a political and religious choice that broke the second commandment and became the lasting sin of the Northern Kingdom
Explain what Isaiah's vision in the temple reveals about the holiness of God and the calling of a prophet
Explain how Hosea's marriage pictures the LORD's faithful love toward unfaithful Israel
Analyze how the prophets brought the LORD's covenant lawsuit against His people by appealing to the blessings and curses of Deuteronomy
Explain the fall of Samaria to Assyria in 722 BC and the reasons Scripture gives for it
Analyze how the prophets joined the call to true worship with the demand for justice toward the poor and oppressed
Evaluate the reforms of Hezekiah and Josiah against the requirements of Deuteronomy and explain why judgment on Judah still came
Apply the biblical tests of a true prophet to the conflict between Jeremiah and Hananiah
Construct a timeline of the kings of Israel and Judah and the prophets who ministered during their reigns
Trace the promises of a coming king from David's line in the prophets of this period and explain how the New Testament reads them as fulfilled in Christ
Evaluate the geopolitical situation involving Assyria, Babylon, and Egypt and the prophets' warnings against trusting foreign alliances instead of the LORD
Defend from Deuteronomy and the repeated prophetic warnings the tradition's teaching that the fall of Jerusalem was God's just judgment
Analyze the theme of the faithful remnant from Elijah and Isaiah to Paul's teaching of a remnant chosen by grace
Produce a study of the Day of the Lord theme in the prophets that traces its near judgments and its final fulfillment

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: Elijah, Jonah, the split, wicked kings, Carmel, causes of division, North and South comparison, categorizing prophets, Jeroboam's calves, covenant lawsuit, fall of Samaria, Hezekiah and Josiah reforms, timeline, geopolitics, the justice of judgment, and the Day of the Lord. Recast the Exile objective as the fall of Jerusalem to leave the exile itself to its sibling. Added missing competencies: God's care for Elijah, Naaman and Elisha, the prophet as God's messenger, Josiah's finding of the Law, Elijah at Horeb, mapping, the ending of Jonah, Isaiah's call, Hosea, justice in the prophets, tests of a true prophet, messianic promises, and the remnant theme. Added verse-level scripture and confession anchors only where a catechism or confession states the doctrine taught.
